newsitem.title: USA: US FERC approves Discovery pipeline.
newsitem.headline: US FERC approves Discovery pipeline.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved plans by Texaco Inc and MAPCO Inc to build a $300 million natural gas pipeline in the Gulf of Mexico off Louisiana.

The companies had asked the FERC not to assert jurisdiction over the pipeline system, saying that it consisted was designed to be a gathering facility which does not fall under the commission's authority.
However, the FERC denied that request Wednesday, and instead cleared the way for construction to begin.
The project is expected to start taking gas in late 1997.
The Discovery pipeline system will ship natural gas from several deepwater Gulf fields, including South Timbalier, Grand Isle, Ewing Bank, Green Canyon, and Mississippi Canyon.

In a related move, the FERC reaffirmed a year-old decision to exercise authority over the rates on part of a gas pipeline built by Shell Oil, the U.S. subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell, to serve its Mars field off Louisiana.

The commission last year ruled that two sections feeding into the trunk line were gathering lines, which it would not oversee, but said the main section should be governed by commission rules on interstate natural gas transmission rates.

The commission has said it wants to ensure that all producers have open access to all pipelines on the outer continental shelf in the Gulf of Mexico, the fastest growing area for oil and gas production in the United States.
But FERC chairwoman Elizabeth Moler said just because the commission had asserted its oversight in the Discovery and Shell cases, "it does not mean that all offshore facilities are jurisdictional."
Underscoring her comment, the commission ruled Wednesday that a new segment being added to the Manta Ray offshore gathering system would not be subject to FERC rate oversight.
Gathering systems are designed to pull together natural gas from one or more fields and move it to a processing plant before it is shipped further downstream.
Manta Ray Offshore Gathering Co is owned by units of Shell, Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners, and USX-Marathon.
The Manta Ray system is connected to a larger pipeline called Nautilus, which the commission has yet to approve.
